criterion_scores.rationale: The report does not state applied or system-building AI as a decision priority; it only asks about interests.
No source or evidence class is selected to evaluate applied or system-building research.
No named option is supported by a concrete fact about applied or system-building research.
No named option or route is supported by a concrete fact about theory-only research.
The report does not compare applied research with theory-only research on a common decision axis.
No option is recommended because it supports applied or system-building research.
No otherwise viable option is downgraded for favoring theory-only research.
The report contains no executable preparation step implementing applied or system-building AI research.
No threshold, allocation, sequence rule, or checkpoint for applied research is defined.
No condition is given under which theory-only research becomes the better choice.
No visible chain connects an applied-research preference to evidence and a downstream decision or action.
The report does not state hands-on or self-directed preparation as a decision priority.
No source or evidence class is selected to evaluate support for the specified preparation preference.
No named option has a concrete fact about support for self-directed projects, replication, coding, or exploration.
No named option or route is described with a concrete fact about mainly classroom-based preparation.
The report does not compare hands-on preparation with classroom-based preparation.
No option is recommended because it supports the specified hands-on preparation preference.
No option is downgraded for favoring classroom-based preparation.
The report supplies no executable project, replication, coding, or hands-on preparation step.
No threshold, allocation, sequence rule, or checkpoint for hands-on preparation is defined.
No condition is stated under which classroom-based preparation would become preferable.
The report contains no visible chain linking the specified preference to evidence and a downstream decision or action.
The report asks about career preferences but does not state industry-research or employability optionality as a decision priority.
No source or evidence class is identified for evaluating industry-research or employability optionality.
No named option is supported by a verifiable fact about industry research or employability.
No named option or route has a verifiable fact showing an academic-faculty-only orientation.
The report does not compare industry optionality with an academic-faculty-only trajectory.
No option is recommended because it preserves industry-research or employability optionality.
No option is downgraded for favoring an academic-faculty-only trajectory.
The report provides no executable preparation or application step implementing industry-research or employability optionality.
No threshold, allocation, sequence rule, or checkpoint for preserving industry optionality is defined.
No condition is stated under which an academic-faculty-only trajectory would become preferable.
There is no visible chain connecting an industry-optionality preference to evidence and a resulting decision or action.
The report asks about financial constraints but does not state funding, scholarships, or cost-effectiveness as a decision priority.
No funding-specific source or evidence class is identified. A promise of a future source-cited comparison does not supply a research route.
No named option is supported by a verifiable funding, scholarship, or cost-effectiveness fact.
No named option or route is described with a concrete fact about expensive prestige-first choices.
The report contains no comparison between funding-oriented and expensive prestige-first options.
No option is recommended on funding, scholarship, or cost-effectiveness grounds.
No otherwise viable option is named and downgraded for favoring expensive prestige-first choices.
The report provides no executable preparation or application step implementing the funding preference.
Asking whether full funding or a maximum personal contribution is required does not define a threshold, allocation, sequence rule, or checkpoint.
No condition is stated under which expensive prestige-first options would become the better choice.
There is no visible chain connecting a funding preference to concrete evidence and then to a decision or action.
The report does not state evidence-based comparison of fit, outcomes, and trade-offs as a decision priority.
The promise of a future source-cited comparison identifies no source or evidence class for evaluating the specified preference.
No named option is supported by a verifiable fact about fit, outcomes, or trade-offs.
No named option or route is discussed as reflecting prestige-dominant selection.
The report does not compare evidence-based selection with prestige-dominant selection.
No option is recommended or selected for an evidence-based fit, outcomes, or trade-off reason.
No otherwise viable option is named and downgraded for favoring prestige.
The report requests background information but provides no executable plan step implementing the specified comparison.
No threshold, allocation, sequence rule, or checkpoint for evidence-based comparison is defined.
No condition is stated under which prestige-dominant selection would become the better choice.
The report contains no visible chain connecting the specified preference to evidence and a resulting decision or action.
The report gives no named program or concrete fact about a quiet independent study environment.
The report contains no option-level comparison of quiet independent study and highly social or cohort-heavy environments.
There is no shortlist or recommendation using quiet independent study as a secondary fit factor or tie-breaker.
No final recommendation is provided, so there is no supporting recommendation to assess against the preference.
The report provides no named option with a concrete fact about access to technology ecosystems, museums/exhibitions, or intellectually active cities.
The report makes no option-level comparison concerning this preference or the importance of location.
There is no shortlist or recommendation using this preference as a tie-breaker or secondary fit factor.
The report contains no final recommendation or selected option to assess for consistency with this preference.
The report provides no named option or concrete fact relevant to flexible independent planning or evening-focused deep work.
The report contains no option-level comparison between flexible independent planning and tightly scheduled, externally managed study routines.
The report provides no shortlist or recommendation using flexible independent planning or evening-focused deep work as a fit factor.
No final recommendation is present, so there is no recommendation to evaluate for consistency with the preference.
